body:
## Outcome

Deliver the agreed militia UI rework across the live campaign flow: navigation, the weekly workspace, setup and corrections, characters and officers, finished weeks, and campaign home. Preserve the application’s existing capabilities, shared play and visual identity while making it easier to use at the table.

This is the implementation parent for the completed [Rework the militia UI for ease of use](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/99) planning map. Its twelve child specs remain the authoritative implementation contracts, including acceptance criteria, prototypes, approved payload/rules changes, compatibility and validation. This parent tracks overall completion and links those contracts.

## Implementation order

Follow the [agreed rollout](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/122#issuecomment-5846600504). The existing native dependencies between children determine which work is unblocked. Start with Navigation shell and keep the app shippable after each delivery; existing editors remain reachable until their specified replacements work.

| Order | Implementation spec |
| --- | --- |
| 1 | [Navigation shell](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/135) |
| 2 | [Week frame](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/137) |
| 3 | [Upkeep](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/140) |
| 4 | [Activity](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/142) |
| 5 | [Event](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/143) |
| 6 | [Persistent](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/144) |
| 7 | [Review & confirm](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/145) |
| 8 | [Setup](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/138) |
| 9 | [Militia corrections](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/139) |
| 10 | [Characters & officers](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/141) |
| 11 | [Finished weeks](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/146) |
| 12 | [Campaign list/home](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/147) |

## Source traceability and future tickets

Trace implementation questions through **implementation ticket → owning area spec → authoring task and original decision discussion → planning map**. The area specs retain direct decision-comment permalinks, later amendments, pinned prototype commits, capability IDs and cross-area contracts.

- [Original UI rework brief, constraints and decision index](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/99).
- [Original capability inventory research](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/100#issuecomment-5828004121) and [baseline inventory PR](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/pull/105); [spec ownership and capability accounting](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/pull/136).
- [Approved split and rollout decision](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/122#issuecomment-5846600504).

When splitting an area spec into implementation tickets in the next step:

1. Attach each ticket as a native sub-issue of its owning area spec, beneath this implementation parent. Put an explicit link to the owning spec and this parent in the ticket body so the source chain remains visible when the ticket is read on its own.
2. Include a **Sources and decisions** section with direct links to the original decision comments and amendments relevant to that slice, plus the authoring task and [planning map](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/99). Copy the relevant pinned prototype links from the spec; a branch name or a paraphrased summary alone is insufficient.
3. Identify the spec acceptance criteria and capability IDs covered by the ticket. Link any other area spec whose contract it consumes and retain native blocking dependencies.
4. If implementation reveals ambiguity, read the linked discussions and explicit later amendments alongside the spec. Cite the exact conflicting sources in the ticket and resolve the ambiguity before changing the agreed behavior. Prototype mock data does not establish rules or expand approved scope.

## Completion gate

Keep this parent open until:

- All twelve child specs are implemented, verified against their acceptance criteria, and closed.
- The capability inventory records actual shipped locations and coverage for all 160 original capability IDs and the new capabilities; removals match the existing explicit approvals.
- Each area’s compatibility, membership/campaign isolation, multi-device behavior and tablet/phone/desktop requirements are verified, including preserved Confirmation and immutable-history contracts.
- Required typecheck, lint and relevant tests pass, with equivalent coverage for the existing E2E scenarios and the implementation evidence linked from the children.

## References and boundaries

- [Capability accounting and ordered spec index](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/pull/136): planned ownership, approved replacements and shared handoffs. Implementation updates the current-location and test evidence as each area ships.
- The planning map stays closed; its decision discussions and later amendments remain the sources of design approval.
- [Add new campaign flow instead of defaulting values](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/94) remains dependent on the Campaign list/home implementation; resolve it when that feature is delivered.
- Scope and exclusions remain those agreed in the map and child specs. This tracking issue adds no design, payload or rollout changes. Prototype branches remain unmerged.


## Implementation progress

- [#149](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/149), [#150](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/150), and navigation-shell area [#135](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/135) completed on local branch `implement/148-ui-rework` through `3088b5a`. All 821 local tests, typecheck and lint pass. The unchanged full isolated-preview nightly gate passes 19/19 on the official Ubuntu Playwright container, including WebKit (`everythingpath-e2e-cSREEF`); native Arch had one WebKit renderer crash on identical source. Astra high Standards and Spec reviews have no remaining findings. Completion comments and the capability inventory record evidence and physical-device limits. Code is not yet merged.
- [#151](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/151) completed through `28506a9`: shared Phase Readiness, responsive Week navigation and compatibility fixes for two reproducible WebKit filter-animation crashes. Typecheck/lint and all 850 tests pass; full isolated-preview nightly `everythingpath-e2e-8ywYlA` passes 19/19 with no skipped gates. Astra high Standards and Spec reviews have no remaining actionable findings; the inventory records actual evidence and physical-device limits.
- [#152](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/152) completed through `1f2d7b8` (application snapshot `69308d6`): read-only Now/After panel, bounded recent history, phone reference sheet and setup-notes dialog. Full 899 tests pass before the final two-file correction; final focused tests, typecheck and lint pass. The full isolated-preview nightly `everythingpath-e2e-fUSm2x` passes 19/19 with exit 0. Independent Astra high Standards and Spec reviews have no remaining actionable findings; actual six-size reference QA and notes/physical-device limits are recorded in the inventory.
- [#153](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/153) and Week-frame area [#137](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/137) completed through `8178b19` (final tested snapshot `9329a66`): shared save/remote feedback, retained week and successor handoff, exact Upkeep address and confirmed-week notice/history link. All 967 tests, typecheck and lint pass; full isolated-preview nightly `everythingpath-e2e-vfgGhJ` passes 19/19 with zero errors and exit 0. Independent Standards and Spec reviews are clear; latest harness reviews use Astra medium. Evidence and limits are recorded in the inventory and completion comments. Code remains local, not yet merged.
- [#154](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/154) is now unblocked and claimed under [#140](https://github.com/AndreasUnunger/EverythingPath/issues/140): Astra medium agents own roll schemas, normalization, rule consumers and boundary tests; Fable 5.1 medium owns compatible UI readers. Existing writers remain until #155. All subsequent Astra reviews use medium reasoning.
